free_tier.stated: 'Free users can download unlimited files per month under 1GB at full speed.' No registration is required; an email is used only to send a licence key.
free_tier.notes: unlimited count, 1 GB per file - the mirror image of TorBox's 10 files at 10 GB

per_object_cap.stated: 'under 1GB' per file on the free tier. Paid is described as unlimited file size; a third-party review puts the premium single-file ceiling near 1.1 TB.
per_object_cap.notes: the 1 GB figure is the only hard number on the vendor page

retention.stated: Not stated on the vendor page. Third-party reviews report a two-day file lifetime on free accounts and seven days on paid.

egress.terms: Free files are downloaded 'at full speed'; no byte allowance is published. Premium is advertised as having no storage or transfer rate limits.

interface_detail: browser only: 'There is no software. Our service works directly through this webpage.' Downloads arrive as HTTPS links from the My Downloads page; no API is documented.
tooling: browser, plus a Chrome extension that posts magnets; Dropbox upload is supported with a user-supplied app token. No API, no CLI.
chaining: the account-free fetch hop: a torrent under 1 GB is fetched and returned as an HTTPS link without signup, which makes it the cheapest way to test whether a tracker or a magnet resolves at all.

limits.value: reported 5 downloads per month on free accounts (Chrome Web Store listing); the vendor FAQ says unlimited

limits_note: the vendor FAQ and the vendor's own Chrome listing disagree on the free download count. The conservative reading is the smaller number, but the FAQ sentence is the one on the homepage.
binding_note: A 20 GiB torrent is 21 times the 1 GB free cap, so size fails before the disputed monthly count matters.

identity_cost.detail: no registration to download: 'Am I required to provide my information or register to use TorrentSafe? No, your E-mail address is only used to send your license key.'

reliability_note: third-party tests report slow transfers and a media player that fails on common formats; the site runs on plain Apache without a CDN and its pricing URL is a 404.
confidence_note: the free-tier sentence and the no-registration claim are from the vendor homepage today. Retention and the monthly count are third-party, and the vendor's own pages contradict each other on the count.

evidence.proved: 'Free users can download unlimited files per month under 1GB at full speed', and 'No, your E-mail address is only used to send your license key'
reported: free lifetime 2 days, premium 7 days, premium from $4.95/month
the extension listing states 'Free users limited to 5 downloads per month', contradicting the homepage

price_per_tb_month: free under 1 GB per file; premium reported at about USD 4.95/month
notes: Included because it is the only service here that returns a fetched file without any account and without a published byte quota - useful as a resolver test even though the 1 GB cap rules out the 20 GiB case.
